request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Pallas by TxPipe: Maintaining Cardano's Core Rust Libraries, Year 2.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 540,750 ADA total, consisting of 525,000 ADA for Pallas maintenance and enhancement plus a 15,750 ADA Intersect budget administration fee.
The motivation text states the grant covers a part-time maintainer for Pallas over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve.

Pallas is described as a collection of Rust crates implementing core Ouroboros and Cardano primitives including CBOR encoding, cryptography, mini-protocol networking, ledger traversal, transaction building, and address handling.
The document claims Pallas is used by projects including Aiken, Dolos, Lucid, Oura, Mithril, Amaru, UTxO-RPC, and others.
The document reports Pallas has over 649 pull requests, 199 stars, 91 forks, 60 contributors, and 214,446 crates.io downloads, with links to GitHub and crates.io.
The proposal claims it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides voting and audit references.
The proposal claims the requested withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
The document states TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

The document states Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based permissions, external oversight entities, and dashboard/on-chain auditability.

The proposal says audit and oversight costs are covered by the overhead and Intersect administration fee, with milestone-based disbursement controls and independent oversight through Intersect and technically capable third parties.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for 12 months of Pallas maintenance by TxPipe, routed through Intersect-managed treasury smart contracts, and presents Pallas as established open-source Cardano Rust infrastructure with stated adoption metrics, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and oversight mechanisms.
